newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: IRISH POUND FIRM VS STERLING, EYES ON BOE MEETING.
newsitem.headline: IRISH POUND FIRM VS STERLING, EYES ON BOE MEETING.

text.p: The Irish pound held firm against sterling in morning trade on Thursday as the market awaited the outcome of the Bank of England monetary policy committee meeting, dealers said.
A decision on interest rates is expected at 1100 GMT but dealers said the market was increasingly expecting no rate change and sterling was suffering as a result.
After recovering some ground late yesterday, it dipped again this morning, losing over two pfennigs to trade just under three marks.
This allowed the punt to clamber up from an opening level of 0.8940 sterling to 0.8970 by 0840 GMT, just above Wednesday's close of 0.8963.
Dealers said mark/Irish continued to be supported by talk of a revaluation.
"We saw good support for mark/Irish yesterday despite the sterling fall. It slipped just a pfennig amid rumours of a possible (punt) revaluation," one dealer noted.
He said such talk was likely to dominate the market in coming weeks, particularly in the run-up to the next meeting of EU finance ministers in September.
"It's anybody's guess really whether or not they revalue. At the end of the day, it's basically a political decision," he said.
This morning the punt stood at 2.6940 marks against 2.6917 at the close and was trading 12.36 percent above the French franc in the ERM grid.
Dealers said the market would keep a close eye on Irish July inflation data, due for release at 1100 GMT, for any signs that Irish pound weakness against sterling was feeding through to inflation.
Concern about rising inflation could be one factor which would prompt the Irish authorities to consider a revaluation, analysts say.
Analysts expect the consumer price index to show a rise of 0.2 to 0.3 percent on the month.
